messages:
talia: heads-up: customer reported split-write rejections after an active-active promotion during an autoscale. client retried and observed inconsistent "write accepted" vs "legal-reject" depending on which replica answered.
omar: ugh. sounds like our steering allowed a write to be routed to a non-resident replica mid-promote.
vik: timeline? did the promotion change shard ownership before routing picked up the new placement?
paul: yes. control-plane marked new-primary in catalog, but routing cache TTLs were 45s. some frontends still sent to old-proxy which forwarded to a shard that didn't accept non-resident writes.
talia: root cause: two separate truths (catalog primary + serving node residency) are out of sync during the narrow window. legal checks only happen at serving layer, routing isn't enforcing residency pre-check.
omar: short-term: lower routing cache TTLs for residency-flagged tenants and add a guardrail to block promotions when cache-miss rate > X.
vik: medium-term idea: introduce a "write-fence" token issued atomically with promotions. token semantics: single valid writer region id + nonce + expiry, signed by control-plane. routing attaches token to write, serving verifies token==its region or rejects. that keeps routing and serving aligned even during cache lag.
paul: love the idea. questions: who mints on scale? we could batch-issue tokens per-tenant session or per-promotion event. we need key distribution for verification.
talia: token TTL should be short (30s-2m) to allow failovers. Also tokens should be opaque to clients and only carried in internal headers, e.g., x-write-fence: <b64>.
omar: perf: ed25519 again? verify per-request could be cheap but at high throughput we'd want local cache of validated token nonces per session. we should avoid per-token DB lookups.
vik: agree. design: control-plane issues token on promotion (or session creation). routing caches token alongside routing entry (same TTL). serving nodes validate signature and compare token.region==their region. on mismatch -> serve rejects and emits detailed telemetry.
paul: fallback policy options: (A) default-deny on mismatch (safe/compliance) (B) default-proxy-backoff and retry to a different replica (availability) (C) log-only in canary. We need cluster-level config.
talia: legal wants default-deny for EU and any tenant with residency_policy=STRICT. ops wants a staged rollout starting with log-only. propose hybrid: log-only global for 48h, then enforce deny for STRICT tenants, and optional deny-by-default in EU clusters.
omar: also surface case for multi-region writes where write must land in an escrow region (customer config). token should carry allowed-regions list (or a single region) but keep token size small. maybe encode region enum + bits.
vik: key rotation: verify keys pulled periodically by routing + serving with overlap window. tokens include key-id header to avoid ambiguity. acceptance of previous key for overlap window.
paul: telemetry: write_fence_mismatch_count, write_fence_verify_fail, write_fence_reject_rate, promotion_blocked_by_cache_miss. Alert threshold: reject_rate > 0.05% for 5m on prod-critical clusters.
infra-bot: Canary run result: active-active promotion canary #7 produced 0.09% write_fence_mismatch events; auto-rollback triggered.
talia: next steps: 1) I will draft an RFC "write-fence tokens for residency-aligned promotions" with sequence diagram + token format + key rotation (talia), 2) Omar will prototype a routing-side token cache and TTL change experiment (omar, 2d), 3) Vik will draft serving-side verification lib and LRU nonce cache (vik, 3d), 4) Paul will add telemetry dashboard + canary plan and default policy matrix (paul).
omar: also adding a temporary guard in control-plane to pause promotions for tenants with residency=STRICT while we finish the token infra. I'll open the PR.
vik: I'll include bench numbers (verify latency w/ and w/out cache) in RFC appendix.
paul: I'll wire an alert and a log-only canary for 72h once prototype lands.
talia: thanks folks. aim to have RFC + PRs in 72h. ping me if you need legal review notes; I'll coordinate with compliance. :thumbsup:
